name: Chat Data API Schema Guide
description:
# Introduction

 Welcome to Chat Data Guide and API Reference, Version 2.0.0!

 Chat Data is a platform that allows you to create AI chatbots using your own data or data provided by the service.
 It offers the following features:

 **Integration**: You can integrate a chat widget or iframe on your website by providing your own documents (.pdf, .docx, .html, .txt), website links, plain text or Q&As.
 
 **Language Compatibility**: Chat Data is designed to work with multiple languages. You can use it with sources in any language and pose questions in any language as well.
 
 **User Analysis**: The owner of the chatbot has the ability to monitor user activities on the chatbot. They can analyze the geographic distribution of users and track user activity.
 
 **Customer Information Gathering**: When customers express interest in the owner's products or services, the chatbot can collect customer information. This allows the owner to gather valuable data for marketing and customer relationship management purposes.
 
 **Email Notifications**: Chatbot owners can receive daily email notifications containing all chatbot conversations and collected leads.

 This reference serves as a comprehensive guide to the [Chat Data](https://www.chat-data.com/) system and
 its Version 2.0.0 API. Here, you'll find detailed information on the objects and
 endpoints used in the API. We greatly value your feedback. If you notice any
 missing or inaccurate information, please don't hesitate to email us at admin@chat-data.com.

 > To leverage Chat Data's API capabilities, you'll need an API key. API keys can be
   created by subscribing to an appropriate membership plan on [chat-data.com](https://www.chat-data.com/pricing).

 ## Conventions

 All API requests should be directed to the domain `api.chat-data.com`, and HTTPS is mandatory for all interactions.

 The Chat Data API adheres to RESTful conventions where applicable, utilizing standard HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE. Request and response payloads are encoded in JSON format.

 HTTP status codes are used in accordance with industry standards. Successful requests return a 200 OK response, while failed requests produce 4xx or 5xx error codes.

 If you have any questions or need further assistance, please don't hesitate to reach out to our [support team](mailto:admin@chat-data.com).

 ## JSON conventions

 * Response body of success requests is generally as follows:

     ```json
     {
       "status": "success",
       "chatbotId": "6650f1c2a9e4b83d2c7a1f05",
       "chatbotName": "Support Bot",
       ...
     }
     ```

     * `status` is a common property.
     * Depending on the API call, there may be other properties as well.
 * A failed response looks like this:

     ```json
     {
         "status": "error",
         "message": "Error message"
     }
     ```

     * `status` and `message` are common properties.

 * Most property names are camelCase; webhook payloads and a few response fields are snake_case, as each operation documents.
 * Optional properties may be omitted or `null`; you can ignore them when they are not needed.

 ## Request limits

 To maintain a uniform developer experience for all API users, the Chat Data API enforces a rate limit of 600 requests per minute (RPM) per workspace. All API keys of the same workspace share that limit. When it is exceeded, the API responds with `429`, a `Retry-After` header and a message saying how many seconds to wait.

 ## Authentication

 Requests use the HTTP `Authorization` header to both authenticate and authorize operations. The Chat Data API accepts bearer tokens in this header. API keys can be managed on your [account](https://www.chat-data.com/account) page.

 ```curl
 curl https://api.chat-data.com/api/v2/get-chatbots -H "Authorization: Bearer $CHAT_DATA_API_KEY"
 ```

 There are two kinds of keys. Workspace keys can access every chatbot and resource in their workspace. Chatbot-scoped keys can access only the chatbot they were created for; operations that are not about a single chatbot (for example `create-chatbot` or `current-plan`) require a workspace key.

 **Please note**: keep your API keys confidential and never put them in client code, including browser HTML and mobile apps. Make API calls from your server.

 # Guides

 Setup guides (training data, Shopify, WordPress, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, webhooks, white label and more) live in the [Chat Data cookbook](https://cookbook.chat-data.com/).
